npmjs.ci-publish: n/a: the page (CI) says a provider should not build a CI publish path on a bypass-2FA token; trusted publishing is held by npm, not by a provider
npmjs.unsupported: n/a: every operation of the protocol has an endpoint on this registry, so there is nothing for the provider to refuse
npmjs.401-erase: n/a: the provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); that exchange is the 401-dead row

gitlab.stage: n/a: GitLab's npm registry page documents no staging or approval step (an absence in the docs, not a documented refusal); a publish is live at once (the page, Staging)

corporate-sso.stage: n/a: the gateway has no staging, no tokens, no teams and no trust endpoints (the page, Publish)

github-packages.stage: n/a: the GitHub Packages npm page never mentions staging and the staged-publishing documents found describe npmjs.com only (an absence in the docs, rechecked 2026-10-20, not verified either way)
github-packages.401-erase: n/a: the provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); that exchange is the 401-dead row

google-artifact-registry.stage: n/a: the pages read for the example describe no staging model (an absence in the pages, not a documented refusal)
google-artifact-registry.not-found: n/a: the docs read do not say the registry hides a repository from an identity that cannot see it; the provider's not-found means nothing stored, and hello registries stops npm asking for unconfigured ones (the page, Rejection)

jfrog-artifactory.stage: n/a: Artifactory has no staged publishing for npm; stage-unsupported.jsonl shows the answer

azure-artifacts.stage: n/a: no Azure Artifacts page read describes staged publishing (an absence in the docs, not proof the endpoints do not exist)

aws-codeartifact.stage: n/a: CodeArtifact has no staging; the page lists stage, stage-read and stage-reject among the unsupported operations

verdaccio.401-erase: n/a: the provider hands out the stored token itself, so after a rejection it holds no other credential to release and the retry can only be `other` (Phase 2, retry rules); that exchange is the 401-dead row
